transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

They sent me here. From the station. ... I was just moving the airway bags. They needed to be in a pattern. The right pattern. I was saying the dispatch numbers out loud, and my lieutenant told me to stop. To step away. But I couldn't. If I broke the sequence, the whole bay would just... it would go bad. So they made me come here.
Have you been feeling unusually elevated or irritable lately?
No. ... I haven't felt like that. I don't really know what you mean. I was just... I just needed to finish the sequence. I feel fine.
Do you believe the sequence has to be done that way because it is truly necessary, or do you think it might be your mind telling you that it has to be done?
...It's necessary. I don't... I don't know why you'd say it's just my mind. It just has to be done that way. That's all.
Do you think this belief might be unreasonable?
No. ... It's not unreasonable. It's just how it works.
Do you want to resist or get rid of this sequence, or does it feel right to you?
I don't... I don't know why I would resist it. It just... it's just what has to happen. I don't want to get rid of it.
Do you ever get unwanted thoughts or images that keep coming into your mind and make you feel you have to do these sequences?
No. ... I don't get thoughts like that. I don't know what you mean by images. I just... I just do what needs to be done.
When you do these sequences, do you feel driven by an inner tension or anxiety that gets relieved only after doing them?
I don't... no. It's not about being anxious. It doesn't relieve anything. I just do it.
Do you ever find yourself doing these sequences to try to stop a thought or fear from happening?
No. I just... I told you, I just do it. It doesn't have anything to do with stopping a fear.
Do you ever hear or see things that other people do not?
No. I just... I hear normal things. I don't really know what other people hear.
Do you think the sequence is definitely true, or could it be your mind playing tricks on you?
I don't... it's not a trick. It's just true. I don't really know what else to tell you about it. It just is.
Do you find this sequence upsetting or distressing?
No, not really. It's just... what I do. It doesn't bother me.
Do you feel driven to do these sequences even though you do not want to?
No. I don't... it's not like that. I just do them. It's not about wanting to or not.
Have you been like this for as long as you can remember?
No. Not my whole life. Just... maybe eight months ago. I hurt my shoulder and ribs during a transfer... an ambulance transfer. It started after that.
Do you ever feel that these sequences are unwanted or against your will?
No. I... I don't really know what you mean by against my will. It's not like that. I just do it.
Do you feel that anything or anyone outside of you is controlling your actions?
No. I don't... I don't think so. No one is controlling me.
Do you think there is any chance at all that this sequence is not truly necessary?

No. It... it is necessary. 

That's actually why they sent me here. I was at the station, and I was just... moving the airway bags. Putting them in a pattern I knew was right. I was saying the dispatch numbers out loud, and... my lieutenant told me to stop. But I wouldn't step away. 

I couldn't. If I broke the sequence... the whole bay would go bad. So... no. I have to do it.
Do other people at the station think the sequence is necessary too?

No... they don't. They... well, I know what they're doing instead. 

The injury review people and... some of the supervisors. I know they watch me on the station cameras. They keep telling me they're just doing routine paperwork, but... I know they're going in and changing my triage notes. They're altering them to make me look unsafe. So... no. They definitely don't think it's necessary. They're just using it against me.
Do you believe the people watching you on the cameras can actually hear or read your thoughts?
No. I don't... I don't think they can read my thoughts. They just watch the cameras.
Have you had similar suspicious or fixed beliefs about other people or situations outside of work?

Outside of work? No. I don't... go out much anyway. 

It's just what I already told you. It's the injury review people. The supervisors. They're the ones watching the cameras and... changing my triage notes. They keep saying it's routine paperwork, but they're doing it to make me look unsafe. That's... that's all it is. Just them.
Have you generally been suspicious of other people’s motives for most of your adult life?
No. I... no. I've never really had a reason to be. It's just... what I told you about the station. That's it.
